newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold - India festival demand falls sharply, seen down.
newsitem.headline: Gold - India festival demand falls sharply, seen down.

text.p: Gold demand in India fell sharply during the traditional Diwali, or Festival of Lights, season and is unlikely to pick up until December, analysts and traders said on Monday.
"Demand fell by at least 20 percent during Diwali and won't pick up until December when the season for weddings begins," M. Damani, president of the Bombay Bullion Association (BSA) told Reuters.
Other traders said it may have fallen by up to 40 percent but did not give give any figures. Demand also fell in other markets like Dubai and Pakistan where sales were poor.

Traders in Dubai, the main gold feeder to the Indian sub- continent, said that gold jewellery and bullion purchases by Indian expatriates celebrating Diwali have been up to 15 percent below last year's turnover.

Sales in the main 22-carat jewellery mart have been depressed by the Gulf state's new residency laws which has led to more than 167,000 workers, mainly from the Indian subcontinent, leaving under a three-month amnesty, traders said.
"Compared to last year it is not as good... People are more hesitant to spend money now because of the amnesty," a leading jeweller said of the Gulf state's tighter labour laws.

The United Arab Emirates has clamped down on thousands of expatriate workers without proper work and residency papers, saying the size of the illegal labour market in the state comprised of seven emirates posed a security threat.
In Pakistan's commercial city of Karachi, dealers said gold prices were expected to ease on low demand due to political uncertainty.
"Most major players are on the sidelines waiting to see the impact of political developments before taking fresh positions," one dealer said.
Last week, Pakistan president Farooq Leghari sacked prime minister Benazir Bhutto citing corruption, nepotism and misrule.
Indian traders said that demand fell because of less money in the hands of consumers and investment being channelled to real estate which showed better returns.
"There has been little purchasing power and there has been a shift to investment in real estate," BSA's Damani said.
Damani said another reason for the poor demand in the weeks to Diwali, which fell on November 10, was because gold buying is not compulsory unlike during the wedding season.
"During the marriage season, gold buying is a must."

Bombay gold prices in the week to November 10 -- markets were kept open on Sunday for auspicious trading -- standard gold (24 carats) rose marginally by 10 rupees to 5,150 rupees per 10 grammes. Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) rose by 100 rupees to 60,200 rupees.
Traders also said they expected prices to be lower in the next few weeks due to weaker world market trends.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion 1$=35.70 Indian rupees, 40.22 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay prices November 10 & 4, Karachi and Dubai prices November 10 & 3 respectively.
-- Feizal Samath, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
